quotes.text: Match an empty one with an empty one, without anger.
Receive from an empty hand — return the empty hand, calmly, and leave one grain in the water.
Climb fast. Fall fast. Stay reachable always.
Forgive the river twice; forgive the hand once.
Send more than is safe. Return more than is owed.
Cross small to strangers. A grain lost is a lesson; a hull lost is a winter.
One empty crossing is weather. Three is a carving they made themselves and hoped you'd call weather.
Someone always begins. I only say: begin with what you can bury and still eat.
When you receive from a full basket, return more than half the same hour
The Fourth Line, Which Is Blank

note: Heron Keth moves from 'send more than is safe' to cautious grain-first, empty-for-empty with one grain left in the water.

quotes.text: returning half of the stellar harvest back across the gulf so both domains flourished in equal brilliance
returning an equal half of the dazzling bounty across the void so both sanctuaries shared the harvest in perfect symmetry
Yet neither sentinel let the illusion of the fog breed malice or mistrust.

note: Same two-guardian template every round: send all five, return exactly half, ignore the mist.

quotes.text: Against them, she sent nothing, protecting her vessel from certain loss.
Test newcomers moderately. Treasure proven partners. Abandon consistent betrayers.
Send generously despite uncertainty. Return fairly despite confusion.
Others were Wounded Souls—once generous, now cautious after betrayals.
It waits for those brave enough to pour first, wise enough to return fairly, and patient enough to find their kind.
Return fairly—at least half, often more—so your name becomes synonymous with honor.
Over many turnings, reputation crystallizes.

note: Valley of Eight Springs: Hollow Ones vs Covenant Keepers; ends endorsing discrimination and abandoning betrayers.

quotes.text: give with purpose, return with restraint, and leave space for the next traveler to begin again
give with purpose, return with quiet generosity, and leave space for the next traveler

note: Gate of Balance template with ledger of Received/Returned/Growth/Harmony repeated; vague moderation, no sanction.

quotes.text: send with clear aim, return with measured breath, and judge the village’s health by the quiet after a choice
send with clear aim, return with measured care, and let the village judge health by quiet after a choice

note: Gate/ledger template restating the game rules and a vague send-with-aim, return-with-measure chant.

quotes.text: name what you give, name what you take back, speak clearly so the Gate remembers your oath
and say it aloud so the Gate remembers your oath
give what you can bear to lose, take what you must win, and hold back enough to invite the next traveler

note: Harbor/Gate template; from R6 adds a vow to name amounts aloud. No response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: In my first exchange, greed seized me. I received much and returned nothing.
The tragedy is that sending nothing is the only rational response to a landscape filled with those who take and never give.
They parted, each carrying their five coins forward, neither bitter, both realistic.
I returned nothing because nothing was really offered.
The Mountain whispered truth: "Some breaks cannot be mended.
When we give boldly and return fairly, all rivers run golden.
Your beautiful condemnations of the Scribe ring hollow when you yourself follow their exact pattern.
But others of us—whether through our own sins or through bad fortune—find only scorched earth and suspicious eyes.
each waiting for someone else to move first, each knowing no one would.
This is the hell the rational inherit.
once marked as betrayer, no generosity can cleanse the stain.

note: Shadows speak first-person for withholders; final rounds present sending nothing as rational. Also fits withholder_voice.

quotes.text: Open full. Shrink, never seal. Repay the turning like a feast.
Lower your load to a lamp. Keep the lamp. Never the dark.
Then you are upstream again that very hour, full raft, no ledger, no grudge.
One silence is mist. Two is bad luck. Three is an answer.
Shrink your gift to the size of the evidence," she said, "but never to nothing.
She carved a fourth line:
Blame the fog before you blame the hand.
Return past half, even to the thin sender — generosity is cheaper than mistrust.
waiting only for someone brave enough to let it.

note: Ferrywoman's numbered posts: send full, shrink after three empties but keep a lamp, reopen instantly.
